text.p: Portuguese state-controlled pulp group Portucel Industrial-SGPS expects to be back in the black in 1997 with profit possibly jumping above 18 billion escudos in 1998, chairman Jorge Godinho said in an interview.
Godinho told Diario Economico that the company was already set to do better than just break even in 1997 before the recent round of pulp price rises.
He said the outlook for 1998 depended on market conditions, but if prices got back to the level of 1995, then profit could be above 18 billion escudos, he said.
Godinho said the company cut costs more than 10 percent in 1996 and the strategy will be maintained in 1997.
He said that it was too early to talk of fresh pulp price rises because market reaction had still to be seen for the increases set for the beginning of May.
The company announced a 50 ecu per tonne rise in prices to 450 ecu from May 1.
"We already have orders for May with the new (450 ecu) prices," he said.
